parts:
Hi!
Hope everyone is doing well. I have a quick question. I want to add a line to my plot, to show the mean, here is my code for my plot:
print(ggplot(ratio9, aes(x = date, y = ratio))+
  geom_line()+
  labs(title = "MA vs V", 
       caption = " Data = tiingo", 
       x = "Date", y = "Ratio of Close Price")+ 
  theme_classic() 
)

I have tried to add the geom_hline(m). 
Everytime I try to add a line after I define the ratio I get an error. Not sure what I am doing wrong. 

Also, is there a way to have two seperate plots on one page?


Also, I am trying to loop the data frames so I can plot multiple plots on different pages. The problem is since I am sourcing my data from an API I have to change the row names to a new column "date". Trying to do this, but I keep getting an error saying "Error in rownames_to_column... is.data.frame(df) is not true"

I tried to loop it to apply, and then also tried Lapply?
Below is my data. 

r <- as.data.frame(SWGAY$SWGAY.Close / CFRUY$CFRUY.Close) 
r1 <- as.data.frame((MOV$MOV.Close) /  (FOSL$FOSL.Close))
r2 <- as.data.frame(FDX$FDX.Close / UPS$UPS.Close)
r3 <- as.data.frame(KO$KO.Close / PEP$PEP.Close)

i <- list(r, r1, r2, r3)

#lapply attempt
chg1 <- lapply(i, rownames_to_column(i, var = "date"), na.rm = TRUE)

#for loop attempt
for(j in i){
  chg <-  rownames_to_column(i, var = "date")
  chg1 <- j %>% 
    mutate(date = ymd(date)) %>% 
    rename(ratio = Ratio)

}



Any help is greatly appreciated. Thank you so much!

>   theme_classic()
> )
>
> I have tried to add the geom_hline(m).
> Everytime I try to add a line after I define the ratio I get an error.
> Not sure what I am doing wrong.

Any chance you could provide a reproducible example (ie minimal code
plus data) which can be copied and pasted to reproduce the error?

Or, at the very least, what is the error message and what is the
code that produces it (ie the ggplot call including the geom_hline
call)?
> Also, is there a way to have two seperate plots on one page?

Yes. Depending on exactly what you are talking about, facet_wrap or
placing grobs in a table would do it. I can't remember where to find
gtable (or is it ggtable?) - grid? gridExtra? GGally? Won't be too
hard to find.

> "Error in rownames_to_column...
> is.data.frame(df) is not true"
>
> I tried to loop it to apply, and then also tried Lapply?
> Below is my data.
>
> r <- as.data.frame(SWGAY$SWGAY.Close / CFRUY$CFRUY.Close)
> r1 <- as.data.frame((MOV$MOV.Close) /  (FOSL$FOSL.Close))
> r2 <- as.data.frame(FDX$FDX.Close / UPS$UPS.Close)
> r3 <- as.data.frame(KO$KO.Close / PEP$PEP.Close)
>
> i <- list(r, r1, r2, r3)
>
> #lapply attempt
> chg1 <- lapply(i, rownames_to_column(i, var = "date"), na.rm = TRUE)

You are calling rownames_to_column with the list i not the data.frame
that is stored in each position of i - hence it fails with the error
above.

Try something like this (not tested):
chg1 <- lapply(i, function(j)rownames_to_column(j, var = "date"), na.rm
= TRUE)

Hope this helps.

Ron.

messages.subject: Re: Adding lines to Graph + plotting two graphs on one plot (how in quantmod you can do mfrow(2,1)
parts: Hi Julia,

> It is difficult for me to give you a snippet of the data, I source it
> from tiingo. Do you have an API key with them? Would be happy to send
> the code then.

No. But you could have easily generated a few random numbers for
a little example. You don't need the 'real' data unless the
problem is only seen with it, a nice small toy example is useful
for people to be able to help you without having access to your
data.

> For now:
>
> m <- mean(ratio9$ratio)
> print(ggplot(ratio9, aes(x = date, y = ratio))+
>         geom_line()+
>         labs(title = "Ratio of UA and UAA Close Price",
>              caption = " Data from Tiingo API",
>              x = "Date", y = "Ratio of Close Price")+
>         theme_classic() + geom_hline(m)
> )
>
> The error I receive is "Error: `mapping` must be created by `aes()`"

Ah. Try changing your geom_hine call to:
geom_hline(mapping = aes(yintercept = m))

geom_hline expects mapping to be the first argument (by default),
and this should be a call to aes, so calling it with the variable
m instead raises an error.

> You are calling rownames_to_column with the list i not the data.frame
> that is stored in each position of i - hence it fails with the error
> above.
>
> Try something like this (not tested):
> chg1 <- lapply(i, function(j)rownames_to_column(j, var = "date"), na.rm
> = TRUE)
>
> Two questions. How did you choose j in function(j)?

I am defining a unnamed function for use by lapply. This has an argument
that I arbitrarily call j (actually becauase you used j in your for loop
example). So j is the current element of i which is being passed tot he
function call and used in rownames_to_column.

> When doing that I receive the error : Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : unused
> argument (na.rm = TRUE)
> Assuming this has something to do with the j  that is used. What does
> this do? Do I need to code something before this?

No, this has to do with me not testing my reply to you and reusing too
much of your code. Try:
chg1 <- lapply(i, function(j)rownames_to_column(j, var = "date"))
Again, this is not tested as I'm not creating a test example to play
with.

I can't see where either rownames_to_column or lapply support na.rm what
were you hoping to achieve by including it your original attempt?

Ron.

This doesn't seem to be a ggplot question anymore.

But I wouldn't be approaching this in this way.

How I would suggest doing it would depend on whether you
want a tidyverse or base R solution, also whether each of
these data.frames has the same dates represented in it and
whether they are all in the same order.

Other comments intersepersed...

I'd be looking to create a data.frame with columns
date, SWGAY.Close, CFRUY.Close, MOV.Close and FOSL.Close.

> r <- as.data.frame(SWGAY$SWGAY.Close / CFRUY$CFRUY.Close)
> r1 <- as.data.frame((MOV$MOV.Close) /  (FOSL$FOSL.Close))
> i <- list(r, r1)
>
> The lapply worked!! What I am trying to do is take these pairs, and
> compare the ratio analysis of X$X.Close from the last day to the 30th
> day before. I figured out the formula to do so, and I want to put it in
> a for loop to just sort of generate a list that shows the greatest move
> over the last 30 days to the least. My code to generate that percent
> change is
>
> j = (tail(i[,2],1) - head(tail(i[,2],30),1))/head(tail(i[,2],30),1)*100

You are using i again, when it is a list with two data.frames in it.
Does this code run? Does it produce the right answer?

What is all the heading and tailing for? why not use nrow to get the
number of rows (eg as N) and address using that and N-30? (Or 29 if that
is appropriate - it lloks to me like your code is getting N-29, 29 rows
earlier).

Something like (for data.frame r) ***UNTESTED***
names(r) <- c('date','ratio')
N <- nrow(r)
(r[N, 'ratio'] - r[N-29, 'ratio'])*100/r[N-29, 'ratio']

Are all days represented - is taking 30 rows before the last always the
same number of days? Might be important if not.

> Now I just need to figure out how to put it in the loop and generate it
> where it takes the absolute value and sorts it automatically!

This isn't really a ggplot2 question anymore so you might want to take
it to the R-help mailing list rather than this one.

Ron.
